name: Does the dry Colorado climate affect interior door painting?

mainEntity.name: Does the dry Colorado climate affect interior door painting?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, the semi-arid climate and low indoor humidity cause paint to dry significantly faster on the surface. While faster drying speeds up recoat times, it can cause water-based paints to dry before leveling out, leaving visible brush marks. Professional painters manage this by working systematically across panel sections and using paint conditioners when necessary. Denver homes also experience wood contraction during dry winter months, making seasonal inspection of joint seams around door casings essential before painting.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, dry Colorado air accelerates surface drying, which requires careful application techniques to ensure paint levels smoothly without leaving brush marks.
